transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the change-control huddle. As you know, we have a firmware retrofit tentatively scheduled for Welding Cell 5 this Friday before the next production run. The controller firmware is reaching end of vendor support this month, so we need to get this done. Before I authorize the work, I need to hear from each of you: controls engineering, what are the technical requirements and risks? Production planning, what do we need to know about the Friday production schedule? And quality, are there any quality validation requirements tied to this firmware change? Let's go around the room.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical. I confirmed with the controller vendor yesterday that there's a safety bulletin identifying an interlock race condition in the current firmware. Because of that, the retrofit must be completed before Welding Cell 5's next production run — this isn't just an end-of-support issue, it's a safety requirement. The work requires exactly 6 hours of energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation. I should also note that the vendor bulletin has not yet been attached to the work order, so we need to get that documented before proceeding.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share important production planning information. My production-capacity check shows that alternate Welding Cell 4 can produce exactly 160 of the 240 assemblies by Friday 16:00. The remaining exactly 80 assemblies must be produced on Cell 5 after the retrofit. However, there's a time constraint: the Cell 4 reservation expires Thursday at noon, and I have not yet entered the temporary reservation in the production system. This means we need to act quickly to secure Cell 4's capacity, and the Cell 5 retrofit must be completed in time to produce those remaining 80 assemblies for the Friday order.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical quality validation requirement. I verified in the customer's quality portal that exactly the first 20 assemblies made after a controller change must be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release. This requirement has not yet been copied into our local inspection plan, so it's not reflected in any of our current procedures. This means that after the Cell 5 retrofit, the first 20 assemblies produced must be quarantined for validation before they can be released to the customer. This directly impacts the 80 assemblies Marta mentioned need to come from Cell 5 — only 60 of those would be immediately releasable, and we need to account for the validation hold time on those first 20.
transcript.speaker: A4
